ath_001: You can recognise it by its trunk walled inside a small stone enclosure of its own. It stands against the west side of the Erechtheion, in the Pandroseion.
ath_002: You can recognise it as the solitary olive standing in a small park. It stands directly behind the Church of Agioi Anargyroi, the neighbourhood's namesake.
ath_004: You can recognise it by its neatly kept trunk standing alone on a traffic island. It stands opposite Evangelismos Hospital, a few steps from the Hilton.
ath_005: You can recognise it by its dense, dark evergreen canopy, unlike the garden's palms and eucalyptus. It stands among the National Garden's quieter paths, away from the pond.
ath_006: You can recognise them by the tall dark cypresses ringing the grounds. They stand around the edges of the First Cemetery of Athens, among the graves and paths.
ath_008: You can recognise it by the staggered rows of olives lining marble-paved paths. It stands across Filopappou Hill, framing views of the Acropolis through the branches.
ath_012: You can recognise it by the large plane canopy shading a taverna's tables. It stands at Diogenous 4 in Plaka, just north of the Roman Agora entrance.
